title: Territorial expansion
hook: Purchases, treaties and war moved US claims west.
notes: Original Orbis factual synthesis; linked federal records and historic-site accounts, checked 14 October 2026. Points locate places approximately, not territorial extents. Modern national/state outlines are reference geography, never reconstructed historical borders. No archival images or source prose redistributed. Sources by scene: Louisiana: the Mississippi gateway: https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/louisiana-purchase-treaty; Across the continent: https://www.nps.gov/subjects/travellewisandclark/expedition-by-date.htm; Texas and the Mexican cession: https://history.state.gov/milestones/1830-1860/texas-annexation; An agreement on Oregon: https://history.state.gov/milestones/1830-1860/oregon-territory; Beyond the contiguous mainland: https://history.state.gov/milestones/1866-1898/alaska-purchase Supplementary date/location evidence: https://www.nps.gov/sitk/learn/historyculture/voices_of_change.htm; https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/check-for-the-purchase-of-alaska. Movement stops/dates: https://www.nps.gov/subjects/travellewisandclark/expedition-by-date.htm. Connecting segments are schematic, not surveyed trails; marker position between dated stops is interpolated. St Charles arrival uses 16 May 1804 from Clark’s journal quoted at https://www.nps.gov/places/st-charles-historic-district.htm ; this detailed source conflicts with its own May 14 summary and the short expedition chronology. The journal quotation is preferred for this waypoint.

scenes.title: Louisiana: the Mississippi gateway
scenes.text: The Louisiana Purchase treaty was signed in 1803. New Orleans locates the river port central to negotiations; this point does not stand for the purchase’s boundaries.

scenes.title: Across the continent
scenes.text: Lewis and Clark travelled west in 1804–1805. Move the dated slider through selected NPS-documented stops: St Charles, Rocheport, Three Forks and Cape Disappointment. The connecting route is schematic.

scenes.title: Texas and the Mexican cession
scenes.text: Texas entered the United States in 1845. The war with Mexico ended with the 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo and a major territorial cession; Santa Fe locates one affected region, not the whole cession.

scenes.title: An agreement on Oregon
scenes.text: The Oregon Treaty of 1846 divided competing British and US claims in the Pacific Northwest. The point locates the Columbia mouth; it is not a treaty boundary.

scenes.title: Beyond the contiguous mainland
scenes.text: The United States purchased Alaska from Russia in 1867. The acquisition preceded statehood by decades and did not mean that Alaska Native peoples had sold their own rights.
